cards.reason: you can't sleep, or it happens before every test.

cards.text: I can't find my library book.
cards.reason: it's been missing for weeks and you're scared to say so.

cards.text: I have to read out loud in class.
cards.reason: you start feeling sick every time it's your turn.

cards.text: My first swim lesson is tomorrow.
cards.reason: you're scared of the water and no one knows.

cards.text: My friend seems mad at me.
cards.reason: it turns into being left out or teased every day.

cards.text: We're moving, and I'll go to a new school.
cards.reason: you feel sad or scared most days for weeks.

cards.text: My grown-ups were arguing, and I keep thinking about it.
cards.reason: anyone gets hurt, or you feel unsafe at home. Then it's Big.

cards.text: I got a bad grade, and I'm scared to show my family.
cards.reason: you're afraid someone will hurt you. Then it's Big.

cards.text: A grown-up asked me to keep a secret, and it feels wrong.
cards.reason: A secret that feels wrong, or that you're told to keep from your family, is always one to tell. That's true even if it's a grown-up you know, or one in your family.

cards.text: Someone at home is very sick.
cards.reason: This is too heavy to carry alone. A trusted adult can help you understand it and help you feel better. It's not your fault, and it's not your job to fix it.

cards.text: Someone online asked me for a photo and said to keep it secret.
cards.reason: Tell a trusted adult right away, even if you already sent something. It's not your fault. The person who asked did something wrong.

cards.text: An older kid hurts me on the bus and says not to tell.
cards.reason: Being hurt is never okay. Someone saying 'don't tell' is a sign to tell. It's not your fault.

cards.text: I've felt worried almost every day for weeks, and it's hard to sleep.
cards.reason: Worry that lasts for weeks, or gets in the way of sleep, school or play, is a sign to get help. Tell a grown-up you trust; a school counselor or doctor can help with worry.

s1: I practiced. I know most of them.
I'll go over the hard ones once more tonight.
One test is one test. I can do hard things.
s2: Lots of kids lose a book. Libraries help find them.
I'll check my backpack, then ask the librarian.
I can tell the truth and fix it.
s3: I can't know what everyone else is thinking.
I'll take a breath and read slowly.
My voice might shake, and I can still do it.
s4: I can ask my swim teacher for help learning safely.
I'll tell the teacher I'm nervous.
Brave means scared and trying anyway.
m1: I don't know that yet. Maybe they're having a bad day.
m2: I made friends before. I can do it again.
I'll say hi to one kid the first day.
New is hard, and I can handle hard.
m3: Grown-ups argue sometimes. It isn't my job or my fault.
I'll tell a grown-up I trust how it made me feel.
I can take care of me right now.
m4: I'll show it and ask what to work on.
Telling the truth takes guts, and I have guts.

clues.name: Head
clues.text: Worry thoughts can loop: what if, what if. They can make it hard to fall asleep.

clues.name: Chest
clues.text: Your heart beats faster. Your body is getting ready to act, like before a race.

clues.name: Lungs
clues.text: Breathing gets fast and shallow. Fast breathing can make worry feel bigger.

clues.name: Tummy
clues.text: Butterflies, or a stomachache. Lots of kids feel worry in their tummy.

clues.name: Hands and shoulders
clues.text: Hands can get sweaty or shaky. Muscles get tight, and tight muscles tell your body it's stressed.
